script.base: Closing line in the pack is Tennessee +7, total 39.5, roof outdoors, kickoff 2026-09-20 13:00 ET, weather not saved. Market script is a modest Philadelphia lead: implied team totals PHI 23.2 and TEN 16.2, so the book expects the Eagles to lead and the Titans to live in the mid-teens. Base flow is Hurts handing the game to Saquon Barkley, who already took 15 of Philadelphia's RB carries for 83 yards in the only 2026 game, with J.Hurts adding 5 designed/scramble rushes for 48 yards, while Will Shipley (2/4) and T.Bigsby (1/3) stay change-of-pace. Pass volume stays secondary: week-1 targets were DeVonta Smith 6, Dallas Goedert 5, Dontayvion Wicks 4, Makai Lemon 4, Barkley 2. Tennessee, down by about a touchdown, cannot live on Tony Pollard's 7 carries for 35 or Tyjae Spears' 3 for 12; C.Ward (4 rushes, 21 yards week 1) will throw more toward Carnell Tate (6/38/67 air), Wan'Dale Robinson (6/38/23 air), Gunnar Helm (5/28/17 air) and Spears (4/12 on -12 air). Those extra Titans dropbacks run into a Philadelphia defense that allowed only 1 of 35 passes to gain 20+ and 3.11 YPA on 19 right-side throws, so this is a grind, not a shootout.
script.flip1: Philadelphia scores first and the lead gets to two scores by halftime. Barkley's carries climb, Hurts' 48 rush yards from week 1 become clock kills, and Smith/Wicks/Goedert routes dry up the way a favorite's WR yards stalled in the skill's DAL 38-21 example. Tennessee abandons the run, Pollard's 7-carry week-1 role shrinks further, and Tate/Robinson/Helm targets rise without PHI paying explosives (1/35 of 20+). A true blowout is only a moderate risk at -7, but it can sit Barkley late.
script.flip2: Tennessee stays within one score or grabs the lead, the 39.5 total drifts up, and Hurts has to throw. That flip cashes the outside overlap: TEN just allowed 4 of 24 passes to gain 20+, 11.67 YPA right and 9.56 YPA left, which is exactly Smith (79 air) and Wicks (79 air). If Cordale Flott (quad, questionable) and linebackers James Williams (elbow) and Cedric Gray (concussion) are inactive, this flip gets worse for every Philadelphia pass under.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the Goedert and Wicks unders both lost. Why? Week 1 was the role. Goedert is the chain-mover who lives near 77 yards, and Wicks is the 4-target explosive who lives near 73, and Tennessee's defense that just allowed 4 explosives, 11.67 YPA to the right and 9.56 to the left could not stop an Eagles offense that posted +0.58 EPA per dropback when not blitzed. Flott was inactive, so the outside overlap actually fired, and Williams plus Gray were out, so the 4.0 middle YPA sample was a one-game mirage. Tennessee blitzed near 27%, Hurts checked down, and Goedert turned those into YAC the way 77 yards on 52 air already showed 25 yards after the catch. The lines were never market prices, just week-1 medians plus 0.5, so there was no edge versus a sharp book. That counter is stronger on the tail than on the median, which is why both stay leans under a flag, and why the slip is pulled if Flott or both linebackers are ruled out before 13:00 ET.
slip_story: One script only: Philadelphia leads on the road at Tennessee, the 39.5 total stays low, Barkley and Hurts run the clock, and the two spike receiving lines do not repeat. Goedert recyds under 77.5 and Wicks recyds under 73.5 win together in that base and in the early-lead flip, and they lose together if Tennessee hangs around. Do not add DeVonta Smith or Wicks overs, a game-total over, or Carnell Tate/Wan'Dale Robinson overs to this ticket; those need flip 2. Do not add Barkley rush over 83.5 just to finish a favorite-runs stack; Tennessee's 4.31 YPC does not support that rung. Do not add Pollard rush under 35.5 as a third leg; the script fits but the rung is too thin against 4 Philadelphia runs of 10+ and Greenard out. This is a two-leg flagged lean pair for the human, not a 3-4 leg posted slip, and it is not a bet.
